newsitem.title: CHINA: China Sinochem foreign trade at $8.53 bln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China Sinochem foreign trade at $8.53 bln in 1996.

text.p: State-owned China National Chemicals Import and Export Co (Sinochem) imported and exported goods worth $8.53 billion in 1996, more than any other Chinese trading firm, the International Business Daily said on Friday.

Imports by Sinochem worth $5.646 billion helped the energy trader top the list of China's 500 highest-value import-export companies for the eighth year in a row, the newspaper quoted the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation as saying.
China National Cereals, Oils and Food-stuffs Import and Export Co was second on the list with exports worth $558 million and imports worth $2.872 billion, the International Business Daily said.
The newspaper added that 27 trading companies recorded international trade worth more than $1.0 billion in 1996.

Large import-export firms were the mainstay of China's foreign trade, although the total value of trade conducted by the top 500 enterprises was down a year-on-year five percent to $126.98 billion in 1996, the newspaper said.
China's total trade was worth $289.903 billion in 1996, up 3.2 percent from a year ago, customs figures showed.
